message.content: Lions (family *Felidae*) and zebras (family *Equidae*) belong to two very different orders—Carnivora and Perissodactyla, respectively. Their most recent common ancestor is therefore the last common ancestor of those two orders, a small, probably insectivorous mammal that lived roughly 60–70 million years ago during the Paleocene/Eocene transition. This ancestor was part of the clade that eventually split into the lineages leading to modern carnivorans (cats, dogs, bears, etc.) and perissodactyls (horses, rhinos, tapirs).
